evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-14"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-14". A POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain calendar date with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 {"dueDate":"2026-12-01"} returned 200 and set the date. PATCH {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and dueDate was null. PATCH /todos/2 with a new date, then with null, then with a date again, all returned 200 and showed the expected values.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "15.10.2026" and "abc" each returned 400. A POST with "2026-10-15T10:00:00" also returned 400. PATCH with "2026-02-30" returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-15 (UTC). Test todos: 2026-10-14 (not done), 2026-10-16, 2026-10-15, no due date, and a done todo due 2026-01-01. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the 2026-10-14 todo. The done past-due todo showed overdue:false after PATCH done:true. The todos due today and in the future, and the one without a date, were overdue:false. GET /todos?overdue=false returned the other four todos, and GET /todos returned all five.
evidence.AC5: The page at / listed the due dates as 14.10.2026, 16.10.2026, 15.10.2026 and 01.01.2026 next to their todos. The todo with no date showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the page only the 'past' todo (14.10.2026) carried the word 'überfällig'. The future, today, no-date and done-past todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list to the single 'past' todo marked überfällig.
